subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: lkj_corr_cholesky is not generating Cholesky factors?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: lkj_corr_cholesky is not generating Cholesky factors?
parts:
On 8/23/13 12:05 AM, Nicholas Nagle wrote:
>
> In general, the densities that are used in the model {} block don't imply any restrictions on things in the
> parameters {} block, but in general the densities typically check whether the restrictions hold. The
> lkj_corr_cholesky() function doesn't actually check whether the input is lower triangular and that is basically
> because it was only intended to be used internally but accidentally got exposed to the Stan parser.
>
>
> OK. Thanks. So, lkj_corr_cholesky should not be used at this time?

Right.

I don't think we can just Cholesky factor a correlation matrix,
because we won't be accounting for the Jacobian. It really does
require us to have a correlation Cholesky factor type.

I just filed an issue to remove it from the function signatures for
2.0.

> What is supposed to happen soon is to introduce a density on L such that L * L' is a correlation matrix with the LKJ
> density, which is probably what you were expecting.
>
>
> Looking forward to this! lkj_corr creates non-positive definite matrices too often for comfort and can take a
> relatively long time per iteration. I was hoping to try out lkj_corr_cholesky, but it sounds like it's not ready.
>
> Again, thanks!

Just a note on what's going on under the hood.

We set things like step sizes to expect a certain amount of
rejection. As long as it doesn't lead to too strong a correlation
in the output traceplots, it's OK in the sense that the posterior
samples are still drawn properly.

The non-positive definite matrices typically arise from arithmetic
issues in either underflow/overflow, non-transitivity of
addition [ (a + b) + c is not necessarily the same as a + (b + c)
in floating point ], and too large a step size in the Hamiltonian
dynamics simulation (which is intentional to get a good balance
between rejection and movement, just as in Metropolis sampling).

- Bob
